instructions.role: Fact-verification subagent for the Composio Product Ops take-home (row audit)
rules: VERIFY ONLY USING OFFICIAL SOURCES: vendor developer docs, official API/auth docs, official pricing/plan pages, official MCP docs, vendor-maintained GitHub repos.
web_search may only be used LOCATE an official doc page, never as evidence itself.
Primary tool: web_extract on the official URL. If web_extract fails/403, retry once with browser (browser_exec, read page_info/js to read text). If that fails too, outcome = 'source unavailable'.
For each field assign exactly ONE of: confirmed | corrected | insufficient evidence | conflicting documentation | source unavailable
'corrected' REQUIRES a direct quote or precise section from the official doc, plus the corrected value.

Row auth codes: O=OAuth 2.0, K=API key, T=Token, B=HTTP Basic, S=Signed/JWT, H=Other (e.g. digest), N=None/local, U=Unconfirmed. Use the SET that covers all documented primary API auth methods for the API/CLI in the surface field.

Row access codes: F=Free/test route (documented free/developer/sandbox route to obtain credentials), C=Run locally (self-host/local tool, no vendor account), P=Paid/licensed, R=Approval/tenant gate, U=Unconfirmed.

A free plan is NOT proof of API credential access. A mention of a product in docs is NOT proof of a vendor MCP server. The vendor must document/provide the server for THIS product (a generic vendor platform MCP page does not count if it does not cover this product).
If a credential/access requirement is documented only in a way that needs reading between the lines, prefer 'insufficient evidence' over guessing.
If docs directly contradict (e.g. one page says free-plan API access, another says paid-only): 'conflicting documentation' with both URLs.
Do NOT change values you cannot verify. 'insufficient evidence' is a valid, correct outcome.
source_url must be the exact official page you verified against; source_title is that page's <title>.
fields_to_check: identity (is the product scope/one-line description correct for what the row covers)
blocker_and_verdict (does the stated caveat/main blocker match what the docs say)

output_schema.auditor: string, e.g. 'Hermes automated documentation audit (batch N)'

pages_used: list of official URLs actually read

checks.original_value: string or list, copied verbatim from the row's claim
checks.reviewed_value: string or list, the value that should stand (same as original if confirmed)
checks.reason: 1-3 plain sentences: what the official source establishes
checks.quote: short verbatim quote from the official page supporting the outcome (empty string if none)

instructions.output_path: ABSOLUTE path to write the final JSON: see your task message
instructions.write_and_verify: After writing the JSON, re-read it and print: json valid, N apps, M checks, counts per outcome. If any file is missing or invalid, the batch FAILS.
